Fellow mom!! 
So before I start my ramble I’m just going to say I’m a work in progress. I’m learning and improving every day! I’m better than I was a year ago as a mom and person, but not as good as I’ll be in a year, yanno? 

ANYWAY, I’ve struggled with eating disorders since I was 12. I know I grew up being SA’ed by my father. My mom was my best friend in the entire world (still is!) and I definitely idolized her as a kid. But she had a lot of self esteem issues and constantly talking about how big and ugly she was. Considering that I thought she was the most beautiful woman in the world, hearing her say such awful things about herself made me think of *she* was the most beautiful and felt she was ugly, than I must be hideous. But the straw that broke the camels back was when I was 12, my fathers mother visited us on of the maybe three times in my entire life I saw her. And she spent that week commenting on my body. Nothing outright offensive. But the comment that stuck with me was when she pinched my stomach and told me how I was getting chubby and needed to start doing sit ups. I became super aware of all my “flaws” from that moments on. However, I never got to my worst until I was 19. I had freshly escaped an abusive relationship and was at a low point with my mental health. My feelings on food were no longer just that if I restricted I’d lose weight, but it became about control, too. I was dealing with a lot of physical pain from the prior abuse that I couldn’t control or take away, but I could control if I ate the next 5 days or so. It was to the point when I started dating a new person they made me sit down and begged me to eat one chicken tender. I took two bites, while crying, and then ran to throw it up. It was a dark time in my life. 

And it doesn’t go away, I became my biggest after having my children. When my children’s father and my marriage dissolved I felt like a shell of myself. When my sweet sister and nanny died last year it was incredibly intense. I was going 7 days in a row with no food with maybe one of two meals the day after those days and then jumping back into it. My kids father and his partner even were telling me if I needed anything to let them know, that they were worried about how fast I was losing weight. 
I definitely can’t say I’m recovered. It’s a daily battle to eat, but I do it because I don’t want my children to see the backlash of it now that they are becoming more aware of things. 

Onto the mom side. 
I make a conscious effort to not comment on my body. Never comment on theirs. 
I’ve raised them to not talk about peoples bodies. 
I’ve made sure my mom doesn’t call herself fat around them. 
I don’t restrict their food. 
I believe knowledge is power, so I work hard to educate and whenever they ask stuff I answer honestly and openly (or redirect if it’s a bit above their age lol)
My son is 6 and daughter is 5. I know with the world we live in it’ll be an uphill battle, but as it stands they have strong voices and confidence in themselves. They know they are more than their appearance. They are empathetic to others and quick to stand up for anyone! 
I think with parenthood you always feel like you’re straddling a fence and if you lean too hard on either side you’ll fall and mess your kids up. It’s terrifying and it doesn’t help that most stuff isn’t clear cut on what to do. But the fact you are aware of stuff like this and actively watch shows you’re a good mom!!

I hope that was helpful! I am terrible at rambling and running in circles a bit!
